content.title: About
content.content: White toasted bread is made from wheat flour, water, yeast and salt, baked and then toasted until the crust turns golden. Toasting creates a crunchy crust while the crumb stays soft and aromatic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasted bread is a common base for sandwiches and appetizers.
The crisp crust results from the Maillard reaction, where sugars and proteins brown under heat.
In many cultures toasted bread is served with butter, garlic or spices.
Toasting reduces moisture, helping the bread stay fresh longer than fresh loaf.
The first electric toasters appeared in the 1920s, making toast accessible to everyone.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: White bread provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation by yeast produces thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Toasting partially breaks down starch, making it easier to digest.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: A crunchy toast serves as a good platform for adding proteins, fats and vegetables, improving the overall nutrient profile of a meal.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White bread can cause rapid blood sugar spikes, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Contains gluten
items.content: The product is unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Over‑toasting can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound; toast to a golden color instead of dark brown.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toast can be spread with butter, jam, avocado, or used as a base for eggs, cheese, ham or vegetable toppings. It also works well as a crunchy addition to soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store toasted bread in a dry place in a paper bag or a ventilated container to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator, though the crust may lose some crunch.
